thread.title: EUROPE MARKETS: European Stocks Rise As Upbeat Corporate Updates Roll In

author: morningstar.com
title: EUROPE MARKETS: European Stocks Rise As Upbeat Corporate Updates Roll In
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
Session's big winners include AMS, Inmarsat, Novo Nordisk
European stocks rose on Wednesday, helped by upbeat corporate updates, as many markets in the region reopened after closing for May Day.
Traders were assessing a downbeat reading on the eurozone's first-quarter economic growth, along with a report on manufacturing activity.
What are markets doing?
The Stoxx Europe 600 index was up 0.6% to 387.28, trimming its year-to-date decline to 0.5%. The pan-European index edged 0.1% lower on Tuesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rise-as-london-sets-tone-on-may-day-holiday-2018-05-01).
The U.K.'s FTSE 100 rose 0.4% to 7,572.98, while Germany's DAX 30 added 1% to reach 12,737.6. France's CAC 40 added 0.1% to 5,525.70.
The euro bought $1.2004, compared with $1.2027 earlier in the session and with $1.1992 late Tuesday in New York.
What is driving the markets?
Encouraging first-quarter earnings from many companies are helping to lift European equity gauges, though investors also have been worried in recent weeks about protectionism and other geopolitical flare-ups.
A softer euro has provided a boost lately to shares in Europe's export-oriented companies. Retreats for the currency, which is still up about 10% against the dollar over the past 12 months, tend to bolster the overseas revenue generated by multinational companies. The shared currency rose above $1.25 in February, but it's lately traded back around $1.20.
Check out:8 reasons to ditch the euro right now (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/8-reasons-to-ditch-the-euro-right-now-according-to-b-of-a-analyst-2018-04-30)
Which economic data are in focus?
The eurozone economy slowed in the first three months of this year, a preliminary reading on gross domestic product showed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/eurozone-economy-wobbles-in-first-quarter-2018-05-02). GDP grew 1.7% on the year, down from 2.7% in the fourth quarter of 2017 and below the 2.5% rate expected. It grew 0.4% on the quarter, as seen, down from 0.6%.
Meanwhile, eurozone manufacturing activity in April fell to its lowest since March 2017, according to a report from IHS Markit. The PMI came in at 56.2, versus a flash reading of 56.0, which was also the level expected.
What are strategists saying?
"The bottom line is that the eurozone expansion remains on track. Growth is moderating from its peak, but still within the range consistent with our baseline scenario of a 2.3% GDP increase this year. However, uncertainty has surely increased, not least because the threat of U.S. trade policies will continue to loom large," said Marco Valli, head of macro research at UniCredit Bank in Milan.
Stocks in focus
Shares in AMS AG (AMS.EB)rose 5% as the Austrian supplier of chips for Apple's (AAPL)iPhones appeared to catch a tailwind from the Silicon Valley giant's better-than-expected earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-were-saved-by-the-companys-new-mvp-2018-05-01) that came late Tuesday. Among other chip makers, BE Semiconductor Industries NV (BESI.AE) shares added 6.1%.

And see: The surprise in Apple earnings -- big growth in China (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-surprise-in-apple-earnings-big-growth-in-china-2018-05-01)
Novo Nordisk A/S (NOVO-B.KO)posted first-quarter earnings that beat forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/novo-nordisk-earnings-beat-forecasts-2018-05-02), but the Danish pharmaceutical company cautioned that despite expecting robust sales growth in the future, intensifying competition and price pressure will have an effect. Shares jumped 5.5%.
Shares in Inmarsat PLC (ISAT.LN)gained 10.2% after the British satellite telecommunications company said pretax profit in the first quarter surged (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/inmarsat-profit-swings-to-net-profit-2018-05-02) versus the year-earlier period.
On the downside, Paddy Power Betfair PLC's stock (PPB.DB)fell 5.5% after the betting company posted a drop in first-quarter profit and revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/paddy-power-betfair-profit-down-to-start-buybacks-2018-05-02).
